title: Parameter optimization of shielded metal arc welding process on weld bead geometry using whale optimization algorithm and grasshopper optimization algorithm
abstract: Abstract The mechanical and microstructural properties of a metal plays a very crucial role in different applications. To obtain the desired mechanical properties, the manufacturing process plays a very critical role. In joining, the weld bead geometry characteristics is there which determine properties. The dimensions of bead geometry characteristics is there which found out the properties. The characteristics depend on and how the process to be carried out. Therefore in this paper, an attempt has been made to optimize the process parameters of shielded metal arc welding (SMAW). The optimization is carried out through whale optimization algorithm (WOA) and grasshopper optimization algorithm (GOA). The significant advantage of algorithms include fast convergence, stochastic, fewer parameters and balance approach between global search and local search. The predicted values of bead geometry is compared with experimental results and it was found that lower error of 0.22% in WOA and 0.28% in GOA as compared to 0.51% in D-optimal error in regression model obtained in the previous data set [ 1 ].
journal: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science

sections.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: In all the processing industry, the transportation, storage, unitizing and identification and storage system plays as crucial role in the industries. The material handling plays a very crucial role in the manufacturing industry. It acts as the robots to provide the components on time. The capacity of the material handling depends on the capability of the material being assembled. So as we focus on quality rather than quantity, the components are manufactured and delivered towards the workstations. If we build the large components, the machine cannot easily accommodate and even the human cannot work it. Large parts and large components are difficult to manufacture. One machine cannot perform all welding tasks. As we are in the era of dissimilar joining, metal, alloys, plastic fibres has to be joined together. So different welding are required, some times different weldings are required for same material. The question is this why we require the welding. If we cast the material, the residual stresses may develop, which could initiate cracks and within few minutes it can reach to hole structure. Whereas, if we perform the welding, the strength of the weld has to be more than the parent material, the crack will not propagate to other part of the structure. So ultimately, the collateral damage is reduced. No its not about higher production, its not about individual brilliance and consistency, its about economics. Which is obtained with quality, utility, availability of the joining process. In the field of joining, SMAW is the process which more profound yet simpler process to implement. It is also called manual metal arc welding (MMA) which can be seen on road side stalls. The name suggest that it cannot be made automatic as other arc welding can be. It utilizes the direct current electrode negative power (DCEN) supply [ 1 ,  2 ]. It has 350 mm long electrode covered with flux coating of different material like rutile, ionic, cellulosic and Inconel which can be used for welding of different materials. With length and diameter of 3.5 mm is placed on the workpiece. The arc is struck due to difference in potential between the electrode and the workpiece, the electrode is consumed and the flux coating on electrode is melted which creates the slag as the shielding layer to provide inert ambient atmospheric conditions to protect the weld pool from oxidation and contamination [ 3 ]. Two types of automation can be achieved, either the electrode holder is moved or the workpiece is moved linearly. In SMAW, the length of electrode is large so electrode holder is set stationary and workpiece is moved which is obtained through lead screw type automation. To obtain the sound weld, fine tuning of parameters are required. This is achieved through techniques like design of experiments (DOE). In DOE, response surface methodology (RSM), factorial design and Taguchi approach is used. Praveen and Vijay [ 4 ] performed the optimization using Taguchi approach in which it has considered L9 orthogonal array with parameters like welding current, welding speed, root gap and position of electrode. The experimentation reveals that welding current and welding speed has higher percentage of contribution in effecting the leakage with values ranging from 54.64 to 22.96. Afzal et al. [ 5 ] performed the optimization in SMAW using grey relational analysis and principal component analysis. It was found that with parameter set of welding current of value 160 A, groove angle of 60°, electrode diameter of 3.25 mm, root gap of 3 mm, and root face of 3 mm, the mechanical properties improved are higher as compared to angular distortion. The higher values of hardness, tensile strength and impact toughness is found more as angular and scalable distortion. Reyes et al. [ 6 ] performed the optimization using Taguchi grey relational analysis approach. The L9 orthogonal array used in experimentation with combination of variable setting of welding current of 130 A, deposition temperature of 300 °C and the duration of heat treatment at 500 °C is 90 min. This set improves the mechanical properties by 149.9% hardness (352 HB) and tensile strength of 1214 MPa. Rahman and Boruah [ 7 ] performed the optimization in shielded metal arc welding using ANSYS. The study reveals the application of set of optimal values of 2.5 mm electrode diameter and current of 250 A adjudging the efficiency of 43.64% and for 4 mm electrode diameter and current of 260 A, the efficiency is much higher i.e. 54.39%. This suggest that with minimal increment of electrode diameter and current the efficiency has increased more than 10%. Singh and Gupta [ 8 ] performed the analysis and optimization of stainless steel 304. The tensile and hardness were estimated. It was found that higher mechanical properties are obtained when welding current has been increased from 90 A to 120 A. This is attributed due to increase in depth of penetration and fusion. Several researchers have implemented the conventional techniques for optimizing the process. These require more calculation and computation time. The recent development of non conventional metaheuristic techniques like WOA, GOA has been implemented in various welding problems. Kannan et al. [ 9 ] performed the WOA of spin-arc GMAW. The optimized values of parameters obtained are 230 A of current, voltage of 24 V, travel speed of 720 mm/min and spin rotation speed of 1500 rpm. The set of parameters changes the mechanical and microstructural properties which includes depth of penetration of 2.5 mm, bead width of 7.7 mm and microhardness of 375 HV. The microstructure is dominated by presence of bainite, martensite and ferrite. Mezaache et al. [ 10 ] performed the optimization of submerged arc welding parameters i.e. arc voltage, welding current, welding speed and wire feed rate using WOA. The results indicate that quality, consistency and neatness along with reduced bead width is obtained. The method is compared to other methods and found to have fast convergence and solution inertness as compared to PSO. Ping et al. [ 11 ] performed the prediction of weld size seam using WOA using robotic arc welding. The optimized parameters includes current, frequency, duty cycle and welding speed. The MAPE of fuse wide forecast is 1.85%. This shows that in terms of percentage error advanced WOA -deep belief network is better than WOA-DBN. The application of WOA in welding is limited but it is applied in path planning of welding robot [ 12 ] and time optimal trajectory planning of manipulators [ 13 ]. Shao et al. [ 14 ] performed the prediction modelling of nugget diameter of weld in resistance spot welding using generalised regression neural network. The model is used as the objective function to find the optimum nugget size. The results indicate that the optimized weld parameters values are comparable with the experimental results. Rasinac [ 15 ] performed the GOA to obtain total yield of welding in GMAW welding using process parameters as seam overhang coefficient, degree of mixing, number of passes and welding current. The results indicate that cost economics is obtained keeping the constrained of maximum permissible cooling rate and maximum permissible hardness of heat affected zone (HAZ). Kahla et al. [ 16 ] performed the optimization of FOPID controller in GMAW process using GOA. The welding current and arc voltage are are two parameters to be optimized. The optimized results are compared with GA and PSO through nonlinear simulation study and some performance indicators. The application of WOA in welding is limited but is applicable in feature selection [ 17 ], power system stability [ 18 ], color feature segregation [ 19 ]. The studies related to application of WOA and GOA in optimization of SMAW parameters has been very limited. As to reduce cost and time with increased accuracy. Therefore optimum prediction of weld bead geometry in SMAW process using GOA and WOA has been implemented. This leads to increased mechanical and metallurgical properties which could lead to have tremendous applications in aerospace, automobile and ship building.

The hysteresis width is the range of welding parameters of shielded metal arc welding process. The welding range has to be obtained by one factor at a time approach or single factor approach. The parameters in this process are welding current, welding speed, arc length, electrode advance angle and joint gap. The lower values of welding current, welding speed, arc length, electrode advance angle and joint gap for welding of 3.15 mm of mild steel is depicted as 100 A, 1.5 mm/sec, 1 mm, 40° and 1.2 mm. This values was obtained from previous literature. Now keeping the other parameters constant, moving the welding current from 100 A to 110 A, then to 120 A and then upto 140 A. After 140 A, the weld bead appearance was there with distortion and warpage and undercut was obtained. This depicts the range of welding current from 100 A to 140 A. Now to find out the range for welding speed, the other parameters and welding current is kept at the lower level, than moving the welding speed from 1.5 mm/sec to 2 mm/sec, then from 2 mm/sec to 3 mm/sec and then to 3.5 mm/sec and simultaneously checking weld bead. Lack lustre weld bead was obtained after 3.5 mm/sec. Therefore the range of welding speed is obtained as 1.5 mm/sec to 3.5 mm/sec. The post deposition stress-relief annealing is required when the range is significantly narrow. In this the range of all parameters are significantly wider depicting the variations in the process. The five level five parameters central composite design is used to optimize and place the experiments.

The Nickel is hard and ductile transition metal known for its corrosion resistance where as manganese is hard and brittle often required for steels. The higher nickel content improves the material machining process thus increasing the strength of the material where as higher manganese content increases the intermetalic zone at the grain boundaries with precipitate. Thus reducing the strength of the material. Therefore higher nickel content in WAAM samples refines the grain boundaries and increases the strength by increasing dislocation density at the grain boundaries. sections.heading: Weld parameter optimization using WOA
paragraphs: The novel WOA algorithm was proposed by Mirjalili and Lewisin [ 21 ]. The WOA is a meta-heuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting technique of humpback whales [ 22 ,  23 – 24 ]. Humpback whales usually prey on shrimps or small fish that swim close to the water’s surface. The whales start swimming around them in a gradually shrinking circle and produce unique bubbles along the route of the circle. The stages of the preying method start with surrounding attack on the prey followed by spiral bubble net development stage, and lastly the random looking for predators. The literature available has been limited. Some of the literature shows that WOA has a tremendous capability of solving complex engineering problems [ 25 ]. Due to its advantages such as simplicity, flexibility, fast convergence speed and stochastic nature, it has gained wide attention among communities of multiple disciplines such as electrical and power systems, data mining and machine learning, wireless sensor network (WSN), network optimization, robotics path planning, training artificial neural network (ANN), cloud computing and IoT, applied mathematics, aero-engine optimization, and skeletal structure design. Some of the striking features of this algorithm includes balanced exploration (global search) and exploitation (local search) strategies of searching and implementation of algorithm with lesser number of parameters [ 26 ,  27 – 28 ]. Moreover it can inherit the efficient function of combining cross-over and mutation process of evolution based algorithm within its structure. This leads to better convergence rate. The drawbacks include alternatively it can get trapped into local optima and fails to apply the global search exhaustively [ 25 ].

sections.heading: Weld parameter optimization using GOA
paragraphs: The GOA algorithm is the metaheuristic optimization algorithm which is been developed by Saremi et al. [ 29 ]. Grasshopper are insects. They are considered a pest due to their damage to crop production and agriculture. Although grasshoppers are usually seen individually in nature, they join in one of the largest swarm of all creatures [ 30 ]. The size of the swarm may be of continental scale and a nightmare for farmers. The unique aspect of the grasshopper swarm is that the swarming behaviour is found in both nymph and adulthood [ 31 ]. Millions of nymph grasshoppers jump and move like rolling cylinders. In their path, they eat almost all vegetation. After this behaviour, when they become adult, they form a swarm in the air. This is how grasshoppers migrate over large distances. The main characteristic of the swarm in the larval phase is slow movement and small steps of the grasshoppers. In contrast, long- range and abrupt movement is the essential feature of the swarm in adulthood. Food source seeking is another important characteristic of the swarming of grasshoppers. As discussed in the introduction, nature-inspired algorithms logically divide the search process into two tendencies: exploration and exploitation. In exploration, the search agents are encouraged to move abruptly, while they tend to move locally during exploitation. These two functions, as well as target seeking, are performed by grasshoppers naturally. The swarm behaviour has been used to solve optimization problems [ 32 ,  33 ] and has been successfully applied for wide range of benchmark and real-world problems [ 34 ,  35 – 36 ] .

sections.heading: Discussion
paragraphs: The higher values of output variables indicate that the whale optimization is successfully applied. Applied. This shows the ability of finding out the food source. The spiralling and encircling the prey is obtained which depicts the limits are being defined and the optimum results are being obtained form that range. On GOA algorithm is based on swarm behaviour of grasshopper which search the through exploration. The team approach is being used to find out the food source. The application of WOA and GOA algorithms work on Darwins theory of natural evolution which equips the survival of the fittest, Where as the GOA works on swarm intelligence. Apart from these algorithms does we have the algorithm like happiness algorithm, cheerful algorithm which is based on the health of the individual, social gathering algorithm, festival algorithms, Energy algorithm, Fear algorithm. All these algorithm are based on survival norms within the society. In the following years we are able to see certain future algorithms which will be based not survival and subsequently finding the food source. Therefor higher values and abundance of the food source is obtained based on the characteristics features of these two algorithms which always find the food source towards team approach and credible sources.

sections.heading: EDS analysis
paragraphs: The welding is obtained which contains homogeneous and uniform structure and elements throughout the fusion zone. The refined structure is obtained where elements remain present in the welded sample. This is supported by the Energy dispersive X ray spectroscopy EDS) which shows that after joining the base material, the homogeneity in the welding is obtained throughout the weld with almost 98% contribution of ferrous alloy and remaining contribution of carbon and manganese with 1.38% and 2.64% depicted in Fig.  12 a and b. The principal alloying element is often evaporated during the welding from the molten weld pool and precipitated at the grain boundaries thus decreases the strength.
Fig. 12 a  Homogenization with Fe of 98.62% and rest is carbon with 1.38%.  b  Homogenization with Fe of 97.36 and rest manganese of 2.64%

The geometric accuracy plays a very crucial role in deciding the cooling rate. Uniform geometry is what is required for effecting cooling rates. Non-uniform geometry decreases the cooling rate. Higher the thickness (> 0.1 mm) fasters the cooling rate as heat dissipation is faster whereas thickness of (0.15–0.6 mm) slows the cooling rate as heat dissipation is slower. This rate of cooling directly effects the mechanical and metallurgical properties of shape memory alloys. The faster heat dissipation brings fine equiaxed and homogenised structure increases the mechanical and microstructural properties of alloys.

In some alloys, slower cooling rates in nickel -rich SMAs (like NiTi) promote the formation of Ni-rich Ni4Ti3 precipitates, which lowers the nickel concentration of the matrix and influences transformation temperatures.

sections.heading: Conclusions
paragraphs: 1. The optimized values of the parameters are within the permissible limits of the boundary conditions through which the better of the fitness values is obtained. 2. The error obtained in WOA and GOA is 0.22% and 0.28% which is lower as compared to the D-optimal value of 0.51% depicted in Table 23. 3. The WOA is evolutionary metaheuristic algorithm which is based on survival of the fittest. This may produce the better results with higher probability of finding the food source. The advantage include fewer parameters, larger dimensions. 4. GOA is there as swarm intelligence which mimics the behaviour of swarm. This is applicable for fast and better convergence, multidimensional decision boundary with balance between exploration and exploitation. 5. The work can be extended further to solve the problems in robotic manufacturing processes.
